chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah; and from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Yūnus al-Shaybānī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: If a drop of blood appears in the nuṭfah? He said: “The drop is one-tenth of the nuṭfah; in it there are twenty-two dinars.” He said: I said: If it drips two drops? He said: “Twenty-four dinars.” He said: I said: If three drops drip? He said: “Twenty-six dinars.” I said: Then four? He said: “Twenty-eight dinars; and for five, thirty. Whatever exceeds the half is calculated accordingly until it becomes an ʿalaqah; when it becomes an ʿalaqah, then in it there are forty.”

Then Abū Shibl said to him—and Abū Shibl informed us, saying: I was present with Yūnus while Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام was informing him about blood-money. He said: I said: What if the nuṭfah came out mixed and stirred with blood? He said, and said to me: “Then it has become an ʿalaqah, if it is pure blood; in that case, there are forty dinars. But if it is black blood, then nothing is due upon him except taʿzīr, because whatever is pure blood belongs to the child, and whatever is black blood, that is from the interior.” Abū Shibl said: If the ʿalaqah has developed something resembling veins of flesh? He said: “Forty-two dinars, one-tenth.” He said: I said: One-tenth of forty is four. So he said: “No, rather it is one-tenth of the muḍghah, because only one-tenth of it has gone; so whenever it increases, it is increased until it reaches sixty.”

He said: I said: If you see in the muḍghah something like a knot, a dry bone? He said: “Then that is bone; thus is the first stage at which bone begins. It begins at five months, and in it there are four dinars. If it increases, then add four by four until it completes eighty.” He said: I said: And likewise when the bone is clothed with flesh? He said: “Likewise.” He said: I said: If he strikes her and the child falls, and it is not known whether it was alive or not? He said: “Far from it, O Abū Shibl. When the five months have passed, life has come into it, and the blood-money has become due.”

key_terms.التَّعْزِيرُ: discretionary punishment when fixed compensation is not due
key_terms.الدِّيَاتِ: blood-money compensations for injury or loss of life
key_terms.النُّطْفَةِ: the seminal drop or earliest embryonic stage
key_terms.الْعَظْمُ: the stage of bone formation in the fetus
key_terms.الْمُضْغَةِ: the chewed-like lump stage of embryonic development
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a dinar, the monetary unit used for the assessed compensation
key_terms.عَلَقَةً: the clinging clot-stage of embryonic development
key_terms.قَطْرَةُ دَمٍ: a drop of blood appearing within the early embryonic matter

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about diyah for miscarriage at different stages of fetal development?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out detailed rulings for blood-money at different stages of fetal development, beginning from the nuṭfah and progressing through the ʿalaqah, muḍghah, and the formation of bone and flesh. It distinguishes the compensation owed according to observable developmental changes and clarifies cases involving blood characteristics and later miscarriage after five months.
